name: Algal growth (green water)
describes: Microscopic algae (phytoplankton) grow in any sunlit, nutrient-fed basin. Their chlorophyll a absorbs strongly in the blue (about 440 nm) and the red (about 675 nm) and weakly in the green, so as they multiply the water turns green and the bed is lost at shallower depth. Per unit of chlorophyll, dense populations absorb less (the pigment-packaging effect), which the measured power law captures. It acts through the whole volume of an outdoor basin; indoors, or under dye, it is held back by the lack of light.

model.text: a_ph(lambda) = A(lambda) Chl^E(lambda), with Chl the chlorophyll a concentration in mg/m3; the chlorophyll-specific coefficient is a*_ph = A Chl^(E - 1).
model.source: J. Meler, S.B. Wozniak, J. Ston-Egiert, B. Wozniak (2018) 'Parameterization of phytoplankton spectral absorption coefficients in the Baltic Sea: general, monthly and two-component variants of approximation formulas', Ocean Science 14:1523-1545, Eq. (3a) and Table A1 (general variant), https://doi.org/10.5194/os-14-1523-2018
model.note: Fitted to about a thousand spectra from Baltic surface waters with chlorophyll a from 0.31 to 142 mg/m3, a range that covers garden ponds; an ocean (case 1) parameterisation would be less apt for a pond.

secchiFromChlorophyll.derivation: Setting TSI(SD) = TSI(CHL): SD = exp((29.4 - 9.81 ln CHL)/14.41)

secchiFromChlorophyll.note: Where algae alone set the clarity. 1 ug/L = 1 mg/m3. The old build's 'bed gone by about 30 cm' corresponds to about 100 ug/L, a hypereutrophic pond.

drivers.text: Light and nutrients drive growth; the dye working removes the light, which is why the Salon pond carries no algae.
drivers.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/

drivers.text: Blue-green algae dominate from about TSI 60 (chlorophyll 20 to 56 ug/L); scums form above TSI 80.
drivers.source: R.E. Carlson (1977) 'A trophic state index for lakes', Limnology and Oceanography 22:361-369 ; equations and class table as given by the North American Lake Management Society, 'Trophic State Equations', https://www.nalms.org/secchidipin/monitoring-methods/trophic-state-equations/

photograph: Green water: the bed fades to olive within tens of centimetres; sunlit water glows green-brown, shaded water looks dark.
Near the edge the colour is strongest where you look down through it onto a pale bed or step.
Late summer ponds are greener than spring ones.

unverified.reason: No measurement of a Suzhou or Beijing garden pond's chlorophyll was found. The canal (clear over a dark bed) and Chenghuai's pond (green) need design values chosen within Carlson's classes; the old build's Chenghuai pond ('bed gone by 30 cm') implies about 100 mg/m3.
No particle scattering coefficient for pond algae was read; the old build's scattering values were set by eye.
